 Concerns Raised Over the Possible Ban of Flavoured Vapes
 St. John's, NL, Canada / VOCM 
 Beth Fagan --> 
 Nov 18, 2026 | 11:45 AM 
 Nathan Burton, owner of Thee Hollow Noggin (VOCM News)
 The regional manager of a vape franchise says he will be forced to shut down almost all of its stores if the government goes ahead with a ban on flavoured vape products.
 Nathan Burton says his company, Thee Hollow Noggin, employs hundreds of people in 26 stores across the province, with most of his products sold as flavoured vape products.
 The government set the wheels in motion to bar such sales, citing concerns about underage access.
 A rally was held at the Confederation Building to oppose the possible ban on flavoured vaping products (VOCM News)
 A protest was held at Confederation Building this morning, where dozens came out to oppose the changes.
 Burton, who says the move took him by surprise, expects more people to switch back to cigarettes.
 “In places like Nova Scotia and New Brunswick, smoking rates skyrocketed as soon as this ban went through. As for vaping, they’re gonna go to the black market,” he told VOCM News.
 “They’re gonna go to drug dealers and other people that are already selling illicit materials, other things that you don’t want your kids near. We are a registered business. We are very strict on our ID policies to make sure that we don’t sell to underage youth.”
